```{r}
data_purchase <- data.frame()
# filter to a needed dependent variable
data_purchase <- appliances %>% 
                  filter(dep_variable_purchase_category == "purschase (probability) of efficient appliance")
# exclude the outliers
data_purchase <- data_purchase %>% 
                  filter(z_value > -0.5,
                         z_value < 0.5)
```

```{r}
# include WTP and purchase probability together
data_purchase1 <- data.frame()
# filter to a needed dependent variable
data_purchase1 <- appliances %>%
  filter(dep_variable_purchase_category %in% c("purschase (probability) of efficient appliance", "WTP for efficient appliance"))
# data_purchase1 <- data_purchase1 %>%
  # filter(!(appliance %in% c("Clothes Dryer", "Dishwasher")))
# exclude the outliers
data_purchase1 <- data_purchase1 %>% 
                  filter(z_value > -0.5,
                         z_value < 0.5)
```

```{r}
# z_value outliers
outlier_z_value <- data.frame()
# filter to a needed dependent variable
outlier_z_value <- appliances %>%
  filter(dep_variable_purchase_category %in% c("purschase (probability) of efficient appliance", "WTP for efficient appliance"))
# exclude the outliers
outlier_z_value <- outlier_z_value %>% 
                  filter(z_value < -0.5 |
                         z_value > 0.5)
# Anderson, Claxton (1982) - fridge - economic - revealed
# Schultz et al. (2015) - very specific intensive intervention - a marketing campaign - lighting - economic - revealed
# Train, Atherton (1995) x5 - confusing modelling - fridge, ac - information - stated
# Li et al. (2021) - fridge - economic - stated
# Skourtos et al. (2021) x4 - fridge - economic - stated
# Ward et al. (2021) x2 - fridge - economic - stated
```

```{r}
# create a list of control variables
controlvars <- c("continent",
                   "statistical_technique",
                   "study_design",
                   "incentive_follow_through",
                   "experimental_setting",
                   "participant_type",
                 "aware_of_study",
                 "opt_in",
                 "randomisation_dummy",
                 "outOfSampleBias",
                 "reportingBiases",
                 "year_publication",
                 "year_data_study",
                 "controls_energy_prices",
                 "controls_environmental_attitudes",
                 "controls_demographics")

appliances$"controls_energy_prices" <- appliances$"controls energy prices"
appliances$"controls energy prices" <- NULL
appliances$"controls_environmental_attitudes" <- appliances$"controls environmental attitudes"
appliances$"controls environmental attitudes" <- NULL
appliances$"controls_demographics" <- appliances$"controls demographics"
appliances$"controls demographics" <- NULL
```


```{r}
# filter by appliance to test basic models

                  filter(dishwasher == 1)

                  filter(refrigerator == 1)
```

```{r}
### RANDOM EFFECTS MODEL ###
##washing machine
m.gen_purchase_washing <- metagen(TE = z_value,
                 seTE = z_variance,
                 data = data_purchase_washing,
                 studlab = authors,
                 sm = "ZCOR",
                 fixed = FALSE,
                 random = TRUE,
                 backtransf = F,
                 )

## forest plot of purchase

png(file = "forestplot_washing_random.png", width = 6000, height = 3000, res = 500)
forest.meta(m.gen_purchase_washing,
           leftcols = c("authors", "Intervention"),
           digits =6,
           col.random = "Red",
           xlab = "Effect Sizes",
           col.square = "Blue")

### FIXED EFFECTS MODEL ###
  
m1.gen_purchase_washing <- metagen(TE = z_value,
                 seTE = z_variance,
                 data = data_purchase_washing,
                 studlab = authors,
                 sm = "ZCOR",
                 fixed = TRUE,
                 random = FALSE,
                 backtransf = F,
                 )

## forest plot of purchase

png(file = "forestplot_washing_fixed.png", width = 6000, height = 3000, res = 500)
forest.meta(m1.gen_purchase_washing,
           leftcols = c("authors", "Intervention"),
           digits =6,
           col.random = "Red",
           xlab = "Effect Sizes",
```


```{r}
### MULTI-LEVEL MODEL ###
# on purchase probability only
# redundant predictors dropped from the model

# Step 1: Create a meta-analysis model
meta_model1 <- rma(z_value, z_variance, data = data_purchase, method = "FE", mods = ~ intervention+0)
meta_model2 <- rma(z_value, z_variance, data = data_purchase, method = "FE", mods = ~ appliance+0)
# dishwasher and heat pump are showing insignificant negative results
meta_model3 <- rma(z_value, z_variance, data = data_purchase, method = "REML", mods = ~ intervention+0)
meta_model4 <- rma(z_value, z_variance, data = data_purchase, method = "REML", mods = ~ appliance+0)
# clothes dryer and dishwasher show insignificant negative results

# Step 2: Fit the meta-analysis model
meta_model5 <-rma.mv(z_value, z_variance, mods =  ~ intervention+0, 
                               random = ~ as.factor(sr_no) | as.factor(study_ID), data = data_purchase, method = "REML")
meta_model6 <-rma.mv(z_value, z_variance, mods = ~ appliance+0, 
                               random = ~ as.factor(sr_no) | as.factor(study_ID), data = data_purchase, method = "REML")
# make graphs from this
summary(meta_model1)
# fixed effects by intervention
# feedback, label, rebate and subsidy significant positive
summary(meta_model2)
# fixed effects by appliance
# AC, light, fridge, tv, washing machine significant positive
summary(meta_model3)
# random effects by intervention
# all apart from loan significant positive
summary(meta_model4)
# random effects by appliance
# AC, light, washing machine, water heater significant positive
summary(meta_model5)
# random effects multi-level by intervention
# all apart from loan significant positive
summary(meta_model6)
# random effects multi-level by appliance
# AC, light, fridge, tv, washing machine, water heater significant positive

# most of the interventions / appliances that do not show significant effects are very small in sample size
```

```{r}
### PURCHASE PROBABILITY + WTP (excl. outliers)
### FIXED EFFECTS ###
meta_model1 <- rma(z_value, z_variance, data = data_purchase1, method = "FE", mods = ~ intervention+0)
# fixed effects by intervention
# feedback, label, rebate, subsidy significant positive
meta_model2 <- rma(z_value, z_variance, data = data_purchase1, method = "FE", mods = ~ appliance+0)
# fixed effects by appliance
# AC, light, fridge, tv, washing machine, water heater significant positive

### RANDOM EFFECTS ###
meta_model3 <- rma(z_value, z_variance, data = data_purchase1, method = "REML", mods = ~ intervention+0)
# random effects by intervention
# feedback, information, label, rebate, subsidy significant positive
meta_model4 <- rma(z_value, z_variance, data = data_purchase1, method = "REML", mods = ~ appliance+0)
# random effects by appliance
# AC, light, fridge, washing machine, water heater significant positive

### MULTI-LEVEL MODEL ###
meta_model5 <-rma.mv(z_value, z_variance, mods =  ~ intervention+0, # add all moderator variables
                               random = ~ as.factor(sr_no) | as.factor(study_ID), data = data_purchase1, method = "REML")
# random effects multi-level by intervention
# feedback, information, label, rebate, subsidy significant positive
meta_model6 <-rma.mv(z_value, z_variance, mods = ~ appliance+0,  
                               random = ~ as.factor(sr_no) | as.factor(study_ID), data = data_purchase1, method = "REML")
# random effects multi-level by appliance
# AC, light, fridge, tv, washing machine, water heater significant positive

### INTERACTION INTERVENTION X APPLIANCE ###
data_purchase2 <- data_purchase1 %>%
  filter(appliance %in% c("Refrigerator", "Air-Conditioner", "Water Heater"))

meta_model7 <-rma.mv(z_value, z_variance, mods =  ~ intervention_category:appliance+0, 
                               random = ~ as.factor(sr_no) | as.factor(study_ID), data = data_purchase2, method = "REML")
# economic incentives x refrigerator have a negative sign  
summary(meta_model3)
```

```{r}
### PURCHASE PROBABILITY + WTP (incl. outliers)
### FIXED EFFECTS ###
meta_model1 <- rma(z_value, z_variance, data = data_purchase3, method = "FE", mods = ~ intervention+0)
# fixed effects by intervention
# all significant positive
meta_model2 <- rma(z_value, z_variance, data = data_purchase3, method = "FE", mods = ~ appliance+0)
# fixed effects by appliance
# AC, light, fridge, tv, washing machine, water heater significant positive

### RANDOM EFFECTS ###
meta_model3 <- rma(z_value, z_variance, data = data_purchase3, method = "REML", mods = ~ intervention+0)
# random effects by intervention
# information, label, rebate significant positive
meta_model4 <- rma(z_value, z_variance, data = data_purchase3, method = "REML", mods = ~ appliance+0)
# random effects by appliance
# AC, light, fridge, washing machine, water heater significant positive

### MULTI-LEVEL MODEL ###
meta_model5 <-rma.mv(z_value, z_variance, mods =  ~ intervention+0, # add all moderator variables
                               random = ~ as.factor(sr_no) | as.factor(study_ID), data = data_purchase3, method = "REML")
# random effects multi-level by intervention
# information, label, rebate significant positive
meta_model6 <-rma.mv(z_value, z_variance, mods = ~ appliance+0,  
                               random = ~ as.factor(sr_no) | as.factor(study_ID), data = data_purchase3, method = "REML")
# random effects multi-level by appliance
# light, fridge, tv, washing machine significant positive


### INTERACTION INTERVENTION X APPLIANCE ###
data_purchase4 <- data_purchase1 %>%
  filter(appliance %in% c("Refrigerator", "Air-Conditioner", "Water Heater"))

meta_model7 <-rma.mv(z_value, z_variance, mods =  ~ intervention_category:appliance+0, 
                               random = ~ as.factor(sr_no) | as.factor(study_ID), data = data_purchase4, method = "REML")
# economic incentives x refrigerator have a negative sign  
summary(meta_model7)

# run a model with control variables included
control_formula <- as.formula(paste("~", paste(controlvars, collapse = "+"), "+ 0"))
meta_model8 <-rma.mv(z_value, z_variance, mods = control_formula,  
                               random = ~ as.factor(sr_no) | as.factor(study_ID), data = data_purchase3, method = "REML")
# contrasts can be applied only to factors with 2 or more levels
# Iterate over variables in the dataset
for (var in controlvars) {
  # Check the number of levels in each variable
  num_levels <- nlevels(data_purchase3[[var]])
  
  # Print the variable name if it has only one level
  if (num_levels < 2) {
    print(paste("Variable", var, "has only one level"))
  }
}
# numeric and binary variables are causing errors

# effects don't change too much from inclusion of 'outliers'
# AC results change quite a bit, although there was only one effect size on AC 
# Train papers show weird results for loan and z_values 
# Skourtos paper has both high variance and z_value
```

```{r}
  pivot_wider(names_from = intervention, values_from = avg)%>%
  print()
```

```{r}
loan <- data_purchase1 %>%
```

```{r}
# Effect level analysis 

ggplot(data_purchase1, aes(x = z_value, y = intervention, colour = intervention)) +
  geom_density_ridges2(fill = "lightblue", alpha = 0.5, scale = .8, 
                       quantile_lines = TRUE, quantiles = c(0.5)) + 
  geom_jitter(height = .1, alpha = .1)

ggplot(data_purchase1, 
              aes(x = z_value, y = appliance, colour = appliance)) +
  geom_density_ridges2(fill = "lightblue", alpha = 0.5, scale = 1, 
                       quantile_lines = TRUE, quantiles = c(0.5)) + 
  geom_jitter(height = .1, alpha = .1)

# Summary by group using dplyr

data_purchase1 %>%                               
  group_by(appliance) %>% 
  summarize(min = min(z_value, na.rm = T),
            q1 = quantile(z_value, 0.25, na.rm = T),
            median = median(z_value, na.rm = T),
            mean = mean(z_value, na.rm = T),
            q3 = quantile(z_value, 0.75, na.rm = T),
            max = max(z_value, na.rm = T))


ggplot(data_purchase1[data_purchase1$opt_in != "no such option",], aes(x = z_value, y = as.factor(opt_in))) +
  geom_density_ridges2(fill = "lightblue", alpha = 0.5, scale = .8, 
                       quantile_lines = TRUE, quantiles = c(0.5)) +
  geom_jitter(height = .1, alpha = .1)
```
